implementation_notes: TypeScript's performance story is the runtime's, so the smell is mostly inherited from JavaScript, with two TS-specific additions. The first is avoiding interfaces and generics because 'they cost something at runtime' — they cost nothing at runtime, since types are erased, so this is an optimisation of nothing. The second is hand-rolling a memoisation or a diffing layer over a library that already has one, usually on the strength of a benchmark for a different workload. The genuine premature choices in TS are bundler-level and worth making early because they are structural: code splitting, tree-shakeable imports, and avoiding a barrel that defeats tree shaking.
idiom_name: avoiding the type system for speed; hand-rolled diffing
pitfalls: Removing type annotations or interfaces believing they affect runtime cost; types are erased.
A hand-rolled memoisation layer over a library that already memoises.
Optimising component re-render behaviour without measuring renders with the profiler.
Choosing a library on a microbenchmark of a different workload, which is the most common form of this smell in TypeScript codebases.
